narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 35% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is above the 10% threshold that requires extra support. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to help you stay on track.

The main reason the model is concerned is your alcohol use on weekdays. Most students your age drink very little or nothing at all during the week, but your level is much higher than average. This was the strongest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. On the positive side, you’ve never failed a class before, which works in your favor. Also, you chose this school for its reputation, which suggests you care about your education—another point in your favor.

However, the concerns about weekday drinking outweigh these strengths. The remedial courses will give you structured time to focus on your studies and create healthier habits. Since you already study more than 10 hours a week and want to pursue higher education, you clearly have the drive to succeed. The extra support is meant to help you channel that effort effectively.

You don’t have to make big changes all at once. Start by reducing weekday alcohol use, as this was the biggest red flag. Keep up your strong study habits and lean on your family for support—especially since your family relationships are currently strained. Small, consistent steps will help you improve your chances of passing the final year.
